title: Carbon cycle
author: Wikipedia contributors
attribution: Wikipedia contributors, “Carbon cycle”, English Wikipedia. Text available under CC BY-SA 4.0; see source history for contributors.
paragraphs: The carbon cycle is a part of the biogeochemical cycle where carbon is exchanged among the biosphere, pedosphere, geosphere, hydrosphere, and atmosphere of Earth. Other major biogeochemical cycles include the nitrogen cycle and the water cycle. Carbon is the main component of biological compounds as well as a major component of many rocks such as limestone. The carbon cycle comprises a sequence of events that are key to making Earth capable of sustaining life. It describes the movement of carbon as it is recycled and reused throughout the biosphere, as well as long-term processes of carbon sequestration (storage) to and release from carbon sinks. At 422.7 parts per million (ppm), the global average atmospheric carbon dioxide has set a new record high in 2024.

To describe the dynamics of the carbon cycle, a distinction can be made between the fast and slow carbon cycle. The fast cycle is also referred to as the biological carbon cycle. Fast cycles can complete within years, moving substances from atmosphere to biosphere, then back to the atmosphere. Slow or geological cycles (also called deep carbon cycle) can take millions of years to complete, moving substances through the Earth's crust between rocks, soil, ocean and atmosphere.

Humans have disturbed the carbon cycle for many centuries. They have done so by modifying land use and by mining and burning carbon from ancient organic remains (coal, petroleum and gas). Carbon dioxide in the atmosphere has increased nearly 52% over pre-industrial levels by 2020, resulting in global warming. The increased carbon dioxide has also caused a reduction in the ocean's pH value and is fundamentally altering marine chemistry. Carbon dioxide is critical for photosynthesis.

sentence.text: To describe the dynamics of the carbon cycle, a distinction can be made between the fast and slow carbon cycle.
sentence.translation: 为了描述碳循环的动态过程，可以区分快速碳循环和慢速碳循环。
sentence.analysis: 句首 To describe... 是不定式短语，作目的状语。主句 a distinction can be made 使用 can + be + 过去分词的情态动词被动结构；make a distinction between A and B 意为“区分 A 和 B”。这里 fast 和 slow 并列修饰 carbon cycle，分别代表下文解释的两类循环。

questions.question: What contrast between fast and slow carbon cycles does the passage emphasize?
options: Fast cycles happen only inside rocks.
Slow cycles never involve the atmosphere.
Fast cycles can finish within years, while slow cycles can take millions of years.
Both cycles always finish within a single day.
questions.explanation: 第二段分别给出 within years 和 millions of years，并说明慢速循环涉及岩石、土壤、海洋和大气。核心对比是完成循环的时间尺度。
hints: 题目比较两类循环，先找两者都涉及的同一种衡量尺度。
第 2 段中分别圈出 Fast cycles 和 Slow or geological cycles 后的时间表达，注意 can 表示可能。

Slow or geological cycles (also called deep carbon cycle) can take millions of years to complete, moving substances through the Earth's crust between rocks, soil, ocean and atmosphere.

questions.question: According to the passage, increased atmospheric carbon dioxide has affected the ocean by doing what?
options: Lowering its pH value and changing marine chemistry
questions.explanation: 第三段写道 a reduction in the ocean's pH value，并接着说 altering marine chemistry。reduction 是下降，不是上升；原文没有“全部移除”或“全部停止”的绝对结论。
hints: 定位海洋变化，不要把大气浓度的变化当成海洋 pH 的变化。
第 3 段倒数第 2 句中，核对 reduction 的方向及 and 连接的另一项影响。
questions.evidence: The increased carbon dioxide has also caused a reduction in the ocean's pH value and is fundamentally altering marine chemistry.

editorialCorrection.text: 原文勘误：第三段的年份与增幅不符。世界气象组织报告，2020 年全球平均大气二氧化碳浓度为 413.2 ppm，是工业化前水平的 149%，即增加约 49%，而非 52%。
editorialCorrection.sourceLabel: 核对依据：世界气象组织 2020 年温室气体数据
